fail_closed_rules: A Water Resources Management Plan is a strategic statutory plan and does not itself grant parcel-level planning permission, land rights or a connection.
A WRMP supply-demand balance is water-resource-zone specific and must not be downscaled into parcel-level water capacity without current company evidence.
A forecast supply deficit is a planning scenario and does not prove an individual development cannot be served.
A forecast surplus is not a guaranteed spare capacity commitment for a particular development or connection date.
WRMP preferred options can change through regulatory, consenting, design and delivery stages; plan inclusion is not project completion.
A draft, revised-draft, final-draft and final WRMP are distinct statuses and must not be merged.
Water-company annual reviews measure delivery against a plan and do not replace the underlying statutory WRMP.
Regional water-resource planning and company WRMPs are related but are not interchangeable legal or evidential documents.
A drought plan sets operational responses to drought and is not a long-term planning permission or permanent capacity statement.
A drought level, temporary use ban or drought trigger is time- and zone-specific and must not be treated as a permanent parcel constraint.
A current dry-weather report is an operational snapshot, not a long-term development capacity forecast.
Drought orders, drought permits and temporary use bans are separate mechanisms and must not be collapsed into one restriction.
An abstraction licence or CAMS resource-availability indication does not create a right for a developer to abstract or connect.
CAMS assessment points and abstraction-strategy boundaries are strategic resource evidence, not detailed parcel hydrology or licence boundaries.
An abstraction licensing strategy boundary is explicitly unsuitable for detailed technical assessment and must not be used as survey-grade parcel geometry.
Environment Agency environmental performance ratings are company-level regulatory evidence, not parcel sewer-capacity evidence.
An enforcement case against a water company does not imply every treatment works or sewer in its operating area is non-compliant.
Absence of a named enforcement case is not proof of full compliance at a specific asset.
A sewage-treatment-works enforcement finding is not a parcel-level planning refusal or development prohibition.
Storm-overflow event data describe discharges and monitoring, not foul-sewer connection capacity for a proposed development.
A storm overflow is not the same asset or function as a wastewater treatment works, pumping station, foul sewer or surface-water sewer.
Storm-overflow policy targets and progress reports are regulatory programme evidence, not parcel-specific discharge consent.
Event duration monitoring data do not measure pollutant load, ecological impact or sewer capacity by themselves.
A DWMP is a strategic drainage and wastewater plan and does not itself approve a connection, requisition, adoption or planning application.
DWMP risk areas, available-capacity assessments and preferred interventions are planning evidence rather than guaranteed engineering capacity.
Draft and final DWMP stages, consultation outputs and subsequent maintenance updates must remain temporally distinct.
Water-company sewer capacity depends on network location, hydraulic conditions, committed growth and current asset data; national guidance alone cannot prove capacity.
Public sewer proximity does not prove a right to connect, sufficient capacity, adoption status or construction feasibility.
Foul-water, surface-water and combined sewer systems are distinct and must not be collapsed into a single sewer-capacity indicator.
Drainage planning, flood-risk drainage and statutory sewerage planning are related but distinct regimes and datasets.
PR24 final determinations set regulatory allowances and outcomes; an allowance is not proof that a specific scheme has started or finished.
PR24 funding or a price-control deliverable does not create planning permission, land rights, procurement completion or asset commissioning.
A delivery plan is a regulatory delivery commitment and not evidence that a named asset is operational.
A PR24 performance commitment definition specifies measurement rules and does not prove current performance at a specific asset.
WINEP actions are environmental programme requirements and do not by themselves identify parcel development capacity or consent.
A WINEP action status must not be treated as completed unless current authoritative delivery evidence supports completion.
RAPID strategic resource options are staged infrastructure development proposals and are not equivalent to consented or operational assets.
RAPID gate progression does not itself prove DCO/planning consent, land acquisition, construction or commissioning.
A proposed reservoir, transfer, reuse or desalination option in a strategic plan does not guarantee the option will be delivered in its current form.
The water-resources National Policy Statement guides NSIP decisions but does not grant a Development Consent Order to a proposed project.
NSIP pre-application, acceptance, examination, recommendation and DCO decision are distinct project states.
A granted water-resources DCO does not by itself prove construction completion, operational capacity or availability to a particular development.
Water-company WRMP documents may redact security-sensitive infrastructure details; absence of public detail is not evidence of no infrastructure.
Water-company WRMP forecasts use stated baselines and assumptions; later housing, industrial or climate assumptions can change future need.
Company-level leakage, per-capita consumption and demand-management targets are not parcel-specific consumption forecasts.
Company service-area or water-resource-zone membership does not prove the exact network connection point or serving asset for a parcel.
Public official datasets may have revision dates, coverage limits and licensing conditions; metadata must be preserved with spatial use.
NO_DATA or unavailable public geometry must remain NO_DATA and must not be converted into evidence that no water or wastewater constraint exists.
Source freshness, legal status and plan version must be checked before mixing 2024, 2025 and 2026 water-resource evidence.
No parcel relation, Future Growth score, business row or promoted source may be created while RECOVERY_PARKED persists and business execution is forbidden.
